title: DS-1000: A Natural and Reliable Benchmark for Data Science Code Generation

en.text: When we measure code-generation models, we reach for benchmarks like HumanEval and APPS: algorithmic puzzles with clean, self-contained prompts. They test whether a model can reason about algorithms, but they look very little like the coding most people actually do, and almost nothing like day-to-day data science. A real data science task is rarely "implement quicksort"; it's closer to "I have this DataFrame and want the inverse of each column added with a matching prefix, the pythonic way."

These are exactly the problems where a model could help most. Data science runs on specialized libraries (NumPy, Pandas, PyTorch), and simply remembering their sprawling APIs is a real barrier for everyday users. Code-generation models could lower it, but the community lacked a benchmark that measures genuine progress. Most existing benchmarks test competition-style algorithms or score answers with surface-form metrics like BLEU, which drift from what a programmer intends as models get stronger: text that looks right scores well even when the code doesn't run.

This ICML 2023 paper introduces DS-1000, a natural and reliable benchmark for data science code generation. It collects 1,000 real problems from StackOverflow across seven widely used Python libraries; it judges answers by executing code rather than comparing text; and it proactively perturbs problems so a model can't pass by recalling a memorized answer. Together, those three ingredients give the field a trustworthy yardstick that is genuinely hard to game.

en.caption: Figure 1. An example DS-1000 problem. The model fills code into the [insert] slot on the left; the completed program is then executed against multi-criteria evaluation, which combines functional test cases with surface-form constraints, with a reference solution shown at the bottom left.

en.text: Paper and code: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.11501 | https://github.com/HKUNLP/DS-1000 | Project page: https://ds1000-code-gen.github.io/
Two problems: the tasks aren't real, and the ruler isn't accurate

Real data science questions almost never arrive as tidy textbook prompts. On StackOverflow, people ask with a lot of context attached: they paste the broken code they wrote, the error message they hit, and concrete input-output examples of what they actually want. That context is precisely what a model should learn to use, yet prior benchmarks strip it away, leaving only an abstract restatement of the task.

The other half of the problem is the evaluation itself. When models were weak, a surface-form metric like BLEU was a passable proxy. But as models improve, the gap between "looks similar to the reference" and "actually runs correctly" only widens: a snippet that closely mimics the reference answer but is logically wrong still scores well. Measuring real progress requires switching to reliable, execution-based evaluation that runs the code against test cases. DS-1000 targets both failures at once: the problems should be natural and carry real context, and the evaluation should be execution-based and reliable.
How it's built: a five-stage pipeline

Turning "wild" StackOverflow questions into problems that can be graded automatically and can't be gamed by memorization is not easy. DS-1000 does it with a five-stage pipeline, and every problem, solution, and metric is cross-reviewed by at least three expert annotators.

en.caption: Figure 2. The five-stage pipeline for building DS-1000: (1) manually select and rewrite high-quality StackOverflow problems, (2) add code context with insertion markers, (3) implement automatic tests (test cases plus surface-form constraints), (4) perturb the original problem to resist memorization, and (5) red-team the evaluation.

en.text: The first stage selects and rewrites problems: annotators keep posts that are high-vote, testable, useful, and representative, then rewrite the colloquial original for clarity. The second stage adds a code context with an insertion marker that tells the model exactly where to write (the [insert] slot from Figure 1). The third stage implements automatic tests: it runs test cases to check functional correctness and also enforces surface-form constraints on the syntax tree, such as forbidding keywords like for/while or specific APIs. The first two stages keep the problems natural; the third makes grading reliable.

The clever part is stage four: perturbation. A model trained on much of the web has likely already seen, and possibly memorized, the original StackOverflow answers. So the authors rewrite each original problem. Surface perturbations change only the wording and leave the reference solution unchanged; semantic perturbations change the intent, so the reference solution changes too; and a batch of deliberately difficult rewrites raises the bar further. Stage five is red-teaming: the evaluation script must reject known-wrong solutions to be accepted. The result is a benchmark that stays close to reality while being hard to pass from memory.
What the data looks like: 1,000 problems with thicker context

DS-1000 ends up with 1,000 problems drawn from 451 unique StackOverflow posts, spanning seven libraries: NumPy, Pandas, TensorFlow, PyTorch, SciPy, Scikit-learn, and Matplotlib. More than half of the problems are modified from their sources to resist memorization: specifically 152 surface perturbations, 235 semantic perturbations, and 162 difficult rewrites.

Statistically, each problem carries on average 1.6 test cases, a prompt of about 140 words, and a 3.6-line reference solution, and 19.4% of problems come with surface-form constraints. That 140-word average is far richer than comparable data science datasets: DSP averages 71.9 words and CoNaLa just 13.8. Longer prompts preserve more of the real, messy context that DS-1000 keeps on purpose and that most other benchmarks quietly discard along the way.
How reliable is the evaluation: accepted answers are almost always right

A benchmark's reliability ultimately comes down to one question: when it says a solution is correct, is it really? The authors quantified this with human review. Among all solutions the benchmark accepts, only 1.8% are actually wrong (the sample-level false discovery rate); among those it rejects, only 0.5% are actually correct (the false omission rate). Put more concretely, DS-1000's problem-level false-positive rate is 5.7%, compared with the 60% reported for the same metric on APPS. Execution-based, multi-criteria evaluation pushes misjudgment down to a very low level.
How the models do: the best reaches only 43.3%

The authors evaluate five pre-trained code models from three families, and DS-1000 separates them clearly. The strongest is Codex-002 in the Insertion (infilling) format, and even it averages only 43.3%, nontrivial but far from solved, leaving substantial room to improve. Across the five models, accuracy ranges from 7.4% up to 43.3%. Notably, the Insertion format supplies right-hand context, and that alone gives Codex-002 a 4.1% average gain over the Completion format, underscoring that infilling genuinely helps on data science tasks. Weaker models such as CodeGen-6B and InCoder-6B fall below 5% on some libraries.
Why perturb: a probe that exposes memorization

Is stage-four perturbation really necessary? The authors ran a revealing probe on the widely circulated numpy-100 problem set. Codex-002 scores 72.5% on the original numpy-100, but once the problems are perturbed its accuracy collapses to 40.6%, and in 36% of the semantic-perturbation cases the model still emits the answer to the original problem verbatim, even though that answer is now wrong. That is the signature of recalling a memorized solution rather than reasoning.

en.caption: Table 1. Accuracy before and after perturbation (Codex-002). A heavily copied set like numpy-100 collapses under perturbation, whereas DS-1000, which is repeated far less online, degrades only gently.

en.text: By contrast, the same perturbation on DS-1000 causes a much gentler drop (about 3.4% for surface and 9.0% for semantic), because these problems appear less often online and leave less room to memorize. The two ends of the comparison make the same point: memorization is a real risk, and deliberate perturbation is a simple, effective defense that keeps the benchmark challenging even for stronger future models.
Takeaway: a realistic, reliable, memorization-resistant ruler

DS-1000 gives data science code generation a rare kind of yardstick: its problems come from real StackOverflow questions, so they stay close to practice; its evaluation runs the code and layers on surface-form constraints, so its scores are trustworthy and rarely misjudged; and its deliberate perturbation blocks memorization, so it is hard to game and stays meaningful as models improve. The fact that even the strongest model reaches only 43.3% is itself a clear marker of how much headroom remains. For anyone working on data science code generation, DS-1000 is both an honest measuring tool and a to-do list that is far from finished.

zh.text: 衡量代码生成模型时，我们习惯用 HumanEval、APPS 这类题目：算法谜题、面试风格、题面干净利落。它们考的是算法能力，却离大多数人真正的写代码日常有点远——尤其是数据科学。真实的数据科学任务往往不是「实现一个排序算法」，而是「我有这样一个 DataFrame，想给每一列加上它的倒数并按前缀命名，最 pythonic 的写法是什么」。

这类问题对模型的价值其实更高。数据科学离不开 NumPy、Pandas、PyTorch 这些专业库，光是记住它们庞杂的 API 就是不小的门槛，而代码生成模型恰好可以帮普通用户跨过这道门槛。问题是：社区一直缺一把能真正量出「进展」的尺子。多数已有基准要么是竞赛/面试式题目，要么用 BLEU 这类表层相似度来打分——随着模型越来越强，这类指标会越来越偏离程序员真正的意图，看着「像对的」文本反而拿高分，可代码根本跑不通。
这篇被 ICML 2023 接收的工作提出了 DS-1000：一个自然、可靠的数据科学代码生成基准。它从 StackOverflow 收集了 1000 道真实问题，覆盖七个常用 Python 库；用「执行代码」而非「比对文本」来判对错；并主动对题目做扰动，防止模型靠背答案蒙混过关。三件事合在一起，给了社区一把可信、且难以被刷分的标尺。

zh.caption: 图1 DS-1000 中的一个示例问题。模型需要把代码填入左侧提示里的 [insert] 处；补全后的程序会被执行，通过包含「测试用例」与「表层约束（surface-form constraints）」的多准则评测，左下角给出一份参考解。

zh.text: 论文与代码：https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.11501 ｜ https://github.com/HKUNLP/DS-1000 ｜ 项目主页：https://ds1000-code-gen.github.io/
问题出在哪：题不真，尺不准
真实的数据科学提问，几乎从不长成教科书里那种干净的样子。在 StackOverflow 上，用户会带着一堆「上下文」发问：贴出自己写坏的代码、报出遇到的错误信息、给出「输入长这样、我想要的输出长那样」的具体例子。这些信息恰恰是模型该学会利用的，可过往基准往往把它们统统删掉，只留一句抽象的题面。
另一半问题出在评测本身。当模型还很弱时，用 BLEU 之类的表层指标凑合还看得过去；但模型一旦变强，「文本相似」和「真的能跑对」之间的裂缝会越拉越大——一段抄得很像参考答案、却逻辑错误的代码，照样能骗到高分。要衡量真实进展，就必须换成「把代码执行起来、用测试用例判对错」的可靠评测。DS-1000 正是冲着这两点去的：题目要自然、要带真实上下文，评测要靠执行、要可靠。
怎么造出来的：一条五阶段流水线
把 StackOverflow 上「野生」的问题，变成能自动评测又不怕被背答案的基准题，并不轻松。DS-1000 用一条五阶段流水线来完成这件事，每一道题、每一份解、每一个评测指标，都至少经过三位有经验的标注者交叉审核。

zh.caption: 图2 构建 DS-1000 的五阶段流程：(1) 人工挑选并改写高质量 StackOverflow 问题，(2) 补上带插入标记的代码上下文，(3) 实现自动测试（测试用例＋表层约束），(4) 对原始问题做扰动以抵御记忆，(5) 对评测做红队测试。

zh.text: 第一步是挑题与改写：标注者按「高票、可测试、有用、有代表性」四条标准筛选帖子，并把口语化的原帖改写清楚。第二步补上代码上下文，用插入标记明确告诉模型「要在哪一处填代码」——也就是图1 里的 [insert] 槽位。第三步实现自动测试：既跑测试用例检查功能是否正确，也在语法树上强制「表层约束」，比如禁止用 for / while 这类关键词或某些 API。前两步保证题目自然，第三步保证判分可靠。
真正的巧思在第四步——扰动。模型见过海量网页，很可能早就「背」下了 StackOverflow 的原答案。于是作者对每道原始问题做改写：「表层扰动」只改措辞、参考解不变；「语义扰动」则改变题意、参考解随之改变；再加上一批刻意加难的「困难改写」。第五步是红队测试：评测脚本必须能挡住已知的错误解，才算合格。经过这一套，DS-1000 既贴近真实，又难以靠记忆蒙混。
数据长什么样：1000 道题，上下文更「厚」
DS-1000 最终包含 1000 道问题，来自 451 个不同的 StackOverflow 帖子，覆盖 NumPy、Pandas、TensorFlow、PyTorch、SciPy、Scikit-learn、Matplotlib 七个库。其中超过一半的题目是从原帖改造而来的，用来抵御记忆——具体是 152 道表层扰动、235 道语义扰动，以及 162 道困难改写。
从统计上看，平均每题带 1.6 个测试用例、约 140 个词的题面、3.6 行的参考解，还有 19.4% 的题目附带表层约束。140 词的平均长度远超同类数据科学数据集——DSP 平均 71.9 词、CoNaLa 只有 13.8 词。更长的题面意味着更丰富的真实上下文，这正是 DS-1000 想保留、而多数基准会丢掉的东西。
评测有多可靠：被接受的解，几乎都真的对

一个基准的可靠性，最终要落到「它判对的，是不是真的对」。DS-1000 用人工复核量化了这一点：在所有被判为正确的解里，只有 1.8% 其实是错的（样本级 false discovery rate）；被判为错误的解里，只有 0.5% 其实是对的（false omission rate）。换个更直观的角度，DS-1000 的问题级假阳性比例是 5.7%——作为对比，同一指标在 APPS 上曾高达 60%。执行式的多准则评测，把「误判」压到了很低的水平。
模型考得怎么样：最强也只有 43.3%

作者用 DS-1000 评测了来自三个家族的五个预训练代码模型。结果拉开了明显差距：表现最好的是 Insertion（插入 / 填空）格式下的 Codex-002，平均准确率也只有 43.3%——不算低，但离「解决」还很远，留出了大量提升空间；五个模型的成绩从 7.4% 一路铺到 43.3%。值得注意的是，Insertion 格式会额外提供右侧上下文，仅这一点就让 Codex-002 相比 Completion（补全）格式平均高出 4.1%，说明「填空式」的代码生成对数据科学任务确有价值。较弱的模型如 CodeGen-6B、InCoder-6B，在某些库上甚至跌破 5%。
为什么要扰动：一次揭穿记忆的探针
第四步的扰动到底有没有必要？作者用广为流传的 numpy-100 题集做了一次探针实验，结果很能说明问题。Codex-002 在原始 numpy-100 上能拿 72.5%，可一旦对题目做扰动，准确率直接塌到 40.6%；而且在 36% 的语义扰动情形里，模型依旧原封不动地吐出「原来那道题」的答案——此时那份答案已经是错的。这说明它是在回忆背下来的解，而不是在真正推理。

zh.caption: 表1 扰动前后的准确率对比（Codex-002）：numpy-100 这类在网上被反复传抄的题集，扰动后崩得厉害；而 DS-1000 因为更少被重复，扰动带来的下降要温和得多。

zh.text: 对照之下，同样的扰动放到 DS-1000 上，准确率的下降要温和得多（表层约 3.4%、语义约 9.0%）——因为这些题目在网上被重复的次数本就更少，记忆的空间更小。这从两头印证了一件事：记忆是真实存在的风险，而主动扰动是一种简单有效的防御，能让基准对未来更强的模型也保持挑战性。
小结：一把真实、可信、抗记忆的尺子

DS-1000 给数据科学代码生成提供了一把难得的标尺：题目取自真实的 StackOverflow 提问，因而贴近实际；评测靠执行代码、并叠加表层约束，因而可信、误判极低；再用刻意扰动挡住记忆，因而难以被刷分、也对未来的模型持续有效。而「即便最强模型也只有 43.3%」这个数字本身，就清楚地标出了这个方向还有多大的空间待填。对做数据科学代码生成的研究者来说，它既是一个诚实的测量工具，也是一份还远未完成的任务清单。

en.subtitle: ICML 2023: HKU, Meta AI, and collaborators build 1,000 real StackOverflow problems with reliable execution-based evaluation

zh.title: ICML 2023 | 数据科学代码生成，需要一把「可信」的尺子
zh.subtitle: 港大、Meta AI 等提出 DS-1000：1000 道真实 StackOverflow 问题，执行式评测，还内建抵御记忆的防线

en.text: When we measure code-generation models, we reach for benchmarks like HumanEval and APPS: algorithmic puzzles with clean, self-contained prompts. They test whether a model can reason about algorithms, but they look very little like the coding most people actually do, and almost nothing like day-to-day data science. A real data science task is rarely "implement quicksort"; it's closer to "I have this DataFrame and want the inverse of each column added with a matching prefix, the pythonic way."

These are exactly the problems where a model could help most. Data science runs on specialized libraries (NumPy, Pandas, PyTorch), and simply remembering their sprawling APIs is a real barrier for everyday users. Code-generation models could lower it, but the community lacked a benchmark that measures genuine progress. Most existing benchmarks test competition-style algorithms or score answers with surface-form metrics like BLEU, which drift from what a programmer intends as models get stronger: text that looks right scores well even when the code doesn't run.

This ICML 2023 paper introduces DS-1000, a natural and reliable benchmark for data science code generation. It collects 1,000 real problems from StackOverflow across seven widely used Python libraries; it judges answers by executing code rather than comparing text; and it proactively perturbs problems so a model can't pass by recalling a memorized answer. Together, those three ingredients give the field a trustworthy yardstick that is genuinely hard to game.

en.caption: Figure 1. An example DS-1000 problem. The model fills code into the [insert] slot on the left; the completed program is then executed against multi-criteria evaluation, which combines functional test cases with surface-form constraints, with a reference solution shown at the bottom left.

en.text: Paper and code: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.11501 | https://github.com/HKUNLP/DS-1000 | Project page: https://ds1000-code-gen.github.io/

zh.text: 怎么造出来的：一条五阶段流水线
把 StackOverflow 上「野生」的问题，变成能自动评测又不怕被背答案的基准题，并不轻松。DS-1000 用一条五阶段流水线来完成这件事，每一道题、每一份解、每一个评测指标，都至少经过三位有经验的标注者交叉审核。

zh.caption: 图2 构建 DS-1000 的五阶段流程：(1) 人工挑选并改写高质量 StackOverflow 问题，(2) 补上带插入标记的代码上下文，(3) 实现自动测试（测试用例＋表层约束），(4) 对原始问题做扰动以抵御记忆，(5) 对评测做红队测试。

zh.text: 第一步是挑题与改写：标注者按「高票、可测试、有用、有代表性」四条标准筛选帖子，并把口语化的原帖改写清楚。第二步补上代码上下文，用插入标记明确告诉模型「要在哪一处填代码」——也就是图1 里的 [insert] 槽位。第三步实现自动测试：既跑测试用例检查功能是否正确，也在语法树上强制「表层约束」，比如禁止用 for / while 这类关键词或某些 API。前两步保证题目自然，第三步保证判分可靠。
真正的巧思在第四步——扰动。模型见过海量网页，很可能早就「背」下了 StackOverflow 的原答案。于是作者对每道原始问题做改写：「表层扰动」只改措辞、参考解不变；「语义扰动」则改变题意、参考解随之改变；再加上一批刻意加难的「困难改写」。第五步是红队测试：评测脚本必须能挡住已知的错误解，才算合格。经过这一套，DS-1000 既贴近真实，又难以靠记忆蒙混。

en.subtitle: ICML 2023: HKU, Meta AI, and collaborators build 1,000 real StackOverflow problems with reliable execution-based evaluation

zh.subtitle: 港大、Meta AI 等提出 DS-1000：1000 道真实 StackOverflow 问题，执行式评测，还内建抵御记忆的防线

en.caption: Figure 1. An example DS-1000 problem. The model fills code into the [insert] slot on the left; the completed program is then executed against multi-criteria evaluation, which combines functional test cases with surface-form constraints, with a reference solution shown at the bottom left.

en.text: What the data looks like: 1,000 problems with thicker context

DS-1000 ends up with 1,000 problems drawn from 451 unique StackOverflow posts, spanning seven libraries: NumPy, Pandas, TensorFlow, PyTorch, SciPy, Scikit-learn, and Matplotlib. More than half of the problems are modified from their sources to resist memorization: specifically 152 surface perturbations, 235 semantic perturbations, and 162 difficult rewrites.

Statistically, each problem carries on average 1.6 test cases, a prompt of about 140 words, and a 3.6-line reference solution, and 19.4% of problems come with surface-form constraints. That 140-word average is far richer than comparable data science datasets: DSP averages 71.9 words and CoNaLa just 13.8. Longer prompts preserve more of the real, messy context that DS-1000 keeps on purpose and that most other benchmarks quietly discard along the way.

zh.caption: 图1 DS-1000 中的一个示例问题。模型需要把代码填入左侧提示里的 [insert] 处；补全后的程序会被执行，通过包含「测试用例」与「表层约束（surface-form constraints）」的多准则评测，左下角给出一份参考解。

zh.text: 数据长什么样：1000 道题，上下文更「厚」
DS-1000 最终包含 1000 道问题，来自 451 个不同的 StackOverflow 帖子，覆盖 NumPy、Pandas、TensorFlow、PyTorch、SciPy、Scikit-learn、Matplotlib 七个库。其中超过一半的题目是从原帖改造而来的，用来抵御记忆——具体是 152 道表层扰动、235 道语义扰动，以及 162 道困难改写。
从统计上看，平均每题带 1.6 个测试用例、约 140 个词的题面、3.6 行的参考解，还有 19.4% 的题目附带表层约束。140 词的平均长度远超同类数据科学数据集——DSP 平均 71.9 词、CoNaLa 只有 13.8 词。更长的题面意味着更丰富的真实上下文，这正是 DS-1000 想保留、而多数基准会丢掉的东西。

en.caption: Figure 1. An example DS-1000 problem. The model fills code into the [insert] slot on the left; the completed program is then executed against multi-criteria evaluation, which combines functional test cases with surface-form constraints, with a reference solution shown at the bottom left.

en.text: Paper and code: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.11501 | https://github.com/HKUNLP/DS-1000 | Project page: https://ds1000-code-gen.github.io/
How the models do: the best reaches only 43.3%

The authors evaluate five pre-trained code models from three families, and DS-1000 separates them clearly. The strongest is Codex-002 in the Insertion (infilling) format, and even it averages only 43.3%, nontrivial but far from solved, leaving substantial room to improve. Across the five models, accuracy ranges from 7.4% up to 43.3%. Notably, the Insertion format supplies right-hand context, and that alone gives Codex-002 a 4.1% average gain over the Completion format, underscoring that infilling genuinely helps on data science tasks. Weaker models such as CodeGen-6B and InCoder-6B fall below 5% on some libraries.

zh.caption: 图1 DS-1000 中的一个示例问题。模型需要把代码填入左侧提示里的 [insert] 处；补全后的程序会被执行，通过包含「测试用例」与「表层约束（surface-form constraints）」的多准则评测，左下角给出一份参考解。

zh.text: 模型考得怎么样：最强也只有 43.3%

作者用 DS-1000 评测了来自三个家族的五个预训练代码模型。结果拉开了明显差距：表现最好的是 Insertion（插入 / 填空）格式下的 Codex-002，平均准确率也只有 43.3%——不算低，但离「解决」还很远，留出了大量提升空间；五个模型的成绩从 7.4% 一路铺到 43.3%。值得注意的是，Insertion 格式会额外提供右侧上下文，仅这一点就让 Codex-002 相比 Completion（补全）格式平均高出 4.1%，说明「填空式」的代码生成对数据科学任务确有价值。较弱的模型如 CodeGen-6B、InCoder-6B，在某些库上甚至跌破 5%。
为什么要扰动：一次揭穿记忆的探针
第四步的扰动到底有没有必要？作者用广为流传的 numpy-100 题集做了一次探针实验，结果很能说明问题。Codex-002 在原始 numpy-100 上能拿 72.5%，可一旦对题目做扰动，准确率直接塌到 40.6%；而且在 36% 的语义扰动情形里，模型依旧原封不动地吐出「原来那道题」的答案——此时那份答案已经是错的。这说明它是在回忆背下来的解，而不是在真正推理。

zh.caption: 表1 扰动前后的准确率对比（Codex-002）：numpy-100 这类在网上被反复传抄的题集，扰动后崩得厉害；而 DS-1000 因为更少被重复，扰动带来的下降要温和得多。

zh.text: 对照之下，同样的扰动放到 DS-1000 上，准确率的下降要温和得多（表层约 3.4%、语义约 9.0%）——因为这些题目在网上被重复的次数本就更少，记忆的空间更小。这从两头印证了一件事：记忆是真实存在的风险，而主动扰动是一种简单有效的防御，能让基准对未来更强的模型也保持挑战性。

en.subtitle: ICML 2023: HKU, Meta AI, and collaborators build 1,000 real StackOverflow problems with reliable execution-based evaluation

zh.title: ICML 2023 | 数据科学代码生成，需要一把「可信」的尺子
zh.subtitle: 港大、Meta AI 等提出 DS-1000：1000 道真实 StackOverflow 问题，执行式评测，还内建抵御记忆的防线

en.text: How it's built: a five-stage pipeline

Turning "wild" StackOverflow questions into problems that can be graded automatically and can't be gamed by memorization is not easy. DS-1000 does it with a five-stage pipeline, and every problem, solution, and metric is cross-reviewed by at least three expert annotators.

en.caption: Figure 2. The five-stage pipeline for building DS-1000: (1) manually select and rewrite high-quality StackOverflow problems, (2) add code context with insertion markers, (3) implement automatic tests (test cases plus surface-form constraints), (4) perturb the original problem to resist memorization, and (5) red-team the evaluation.

en.text: The first stage selects and rewrites problems: annotators keep posts that are high-vote, testable, useful, and representative, then rewrite the colloquial original for clarity. The second stage adds a code context with an insertion marker that tells the model exactly where to write (the [insert] slot from Figure 1). The third stage implements automatic tests: it runs test cases to check functional correctness and also enforces surface-form constraints on the syntax tree, such as forbidding keywords like for/while or specific APIs. The first two stages keep the problems natural; the third makes grading reliable.

The clever part is stage four: perturbation. A model trained on much of the web has likely already seen, and possibly memorized, the original StackOverflow answers. So the authors rewrite each original problem. Surface perturbations change only the wording and leave the reference solution unchanged; semantic perturbations change the intent, so the reference solution changes too; and a batch of deliberately difficult rewrites raises the bar further. Stage five is red-teaming: the evaluation script must reject known-wrong solutions to be accepted. The result is a benchmark that stays close to reality while being hard to pass from memory.

en.caption: Figure 1. An example DS-1000 problem. The model fills code into the [insert] slot on the left; the completed program is then executed against multi-criteria evaluation, which combines functional test cases with surface-form constraints, with a reference solution shown at the bottom left.

en.text: Why perturb: a probe that exposes memorization

Is stage-four perturbation really necessary? The authors ran a revealing probe on the widely circulated numpy-100 problem set. Codex-002 scores 72.5% on the original numpy-100, but once the problems are perturbed its accuracy collapses to 40.6%, and in 36% of the semantic-perturbation cases the model still emits the answer to the original problem verbatim, even though that answer is now wrong. That is the signature of recalling a memorized solution rather than reasoning.

en.caption: Table 1. Accuracy before and after perturbation (Codex-002). A heavily copied set like numpy-100 collapses under perturbation, whereas DS-1000, which is repeated far less online, degrades only gently.

en.text: By contrast, the same perturbation on DS-1000 causes a much gentler drop (about 3.4% for surface and 9.0% for semantic), because these problems appear less often online and leave less room to memorize. The two ends of the comparison make the same point: memorization is a real risk, and deliberate perturbation is a simple, effective defense that keeps the benchmark challenging even for stronger future models.
Takeaway: a realistic, reliable, memorization-resistant ruler

DS-1000 gives data science code generation a rare kind of yardstick: its problems come from real StackOverflow questions, so they stay close to practice; its evaluation runs the code and layers on surface-form constraints, so its scores are trustworthy and rarely misjudged; and its deliberate perturbation blocks memorization, so it is hard to game and stays meaningful as models improve. The fact that even the strongest model reaches only 43.3% is itself a clear marker of how much headroom remains. For anyone working on data science code generation, DS-1000 is both an honest measuring tool and a to-do list that is far from finished.

第四步的扰动到底有没有必要？作者用广为流传的 numpy-100 题集做了一次探针实验，结果很能说明问题。Codex-002 在原始 numpy-100 上能拿 72.5%，可一旦对题目做扰动，准确率直接塌到 40.6%；而且在 36% 的语义扰动情形里，模型依旧原封不动地吐出「原来那道题」的答案——此时那份答案已经是错的。这说明它是在回忆背下来的解，而不是在真正推理。

zh.caption: 表1 扰动前后的准确率对比（Codex-002）：numpy-100 这类在网上被反复传抄的题集，扰动后崩得厉害；而 DS-1000 因为更少被重复，扰动带来的下降要温和得多。

zh.text: 对照之下，同样的扰动放到 DS-1000 上，准确率的下降要温和得多（表层约 3.4%、语义约 9.0%）——因为这些题目在网上被重复的次数本就更少，记忆的空间更小。这从两头印证了一件事：记忆是真实存在的风险，而主动扰动是一种简单有效的防御，能让基准对未来更强的模型也保持挑战性。
小结：一把真实、可信、抗记忆的尺子

DS-1000 给数据科学代码生成提供了一把难得的标尺：题目取自真实的 StackOverflow 提问，因而贴近实际；评测靠执行代码、并叠加表层约束，因而可信、误判极低；再用刻意扰动挡住记忆，因而难以被刷分、也对未来的模型持续有效。而「即便最强模型也只有 43.3%」这个数字本身，就清楚地标出了这个方向还有多大的空间待填。对做数据科学代码生成的研究者来说，它既是一个诚实的测量工具，也是一份还远未完成的任务清单。
